item.title: Jeff Bezos’ Earth Fund adds $25 million for Pacific Ocean conservation
item.description: The Bezos Earth Fund is allocating more than $25 million for ocean conservation projects in five Pacific nations. This funding will support various efforts: enhancing ocean management, establishing marine protected areas, and improving monitoring. The initiative aims to protect a significant portion of the ocean while promoting local leadership and community involvement. Additionally, international waters will also benefit from proposed marine protected areas.

item.title: Straitcraft: How geography gives Iran leverage and could do the same for India
item.description: Since the onset of the US-Iran war over 200 days ago, Iran has been strategically utilizing maritime chokepoints such as Hormuz. This has resulted in a marked decline in oil flows, affecting the global economy and forcing the US to reconsider its stance. Concurrently, India is exploring ways to capitalize on its geographical advantages against China.

item.title: Colorado couple closes family restaurant after 31 years as children build careers
item.description: A Colorado couple who moved from Mexico in 1995 with their three children opened Los Tarascos and ran it for 31 years. Jose and Maria Caballero are now closing the Fort Collins restaurant, saying they have achieved the dream that brought them to the US: giving their children the chance to build independent lives and careers outside the family business.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Nokia closes China research hub; recalls CEO’s Huawei warning to Europe
item.description: Nokia is shutting its Hangzhou radio R&D centre in China by end-2026, cutting around 1,600 jobs, after its Greater China revenue fell over 58% since 2018. The closure revives CEO Justin Hotard's pointed question to Europe: why does Huawei still run nearly 60% of Germany's 5G sites while Nokia holds under 3% share in China? Restructuring charges have tripled to €800 million, even as AI and cloud orders surge 105%.

item.title: Michael Tilson Thomas bought SF mansion for $1.4m; 32 years later, it asks $10m
item.description: Michael Tilson Thomas’s residence in Pacific Heights is now on the market following his passing earlier this year. The mansion was a sanctuary for the musician and his husband Joshua Robison for nearly three decades. Built in 1906, the four-level home features a blend of architectural styles and modern amenities added over the years. Its spacious rooms hosted numerous distinguished guests from the music and architecture worlds.

item.title: Alonzo Mourning’s $37.4M affordable housing project offers $322 senior homes
item.description: After his NBA career, Alonzo Mourning founded AM Affordable Housing to address the pressing need for affordable homes in South Florida. Through collaboration with Housing Trust Group, he has spearheaded various projects, including the Astoria on 9th, which boasts 120 affordable apartments in Bradenton. With overwhelming demand and countless applicants vying for limited options, Mourning draws on his foster care history to fuel his philanthropic mission.

item.title: 'No eligible elector will be left behind': Goa CEO clarifies on 97 missing voters
item.description: The Chief Electoral Officer of Goa has provided clarity regarding the exclusion of 97 voters from the electoral rolls. These individuals were initially identified due to discrepancies reported during the Special Intensive Revision process. However, follow-up house visits successfully registered many eligible voters. This incident has raised concerns over the reliability of the Election Commission's ECINet software, prompting criticism from opposition parties about electoral registration procedures and centralization.

item.description: Russell Wilson and Ciara have spent more than a decade using their Why Not You Foundation to support children through education, health care and hunger programs. Their work includes a $1.75 million school investment, a $3 million hospital gift, a $2 million donation in Mexico and $500,000 for Atlanta food programs, along with wider fundraising and youth programs.

item.title: Did AI-‘kill chain’ lead to deadly Iran school strike? What report claims
item.description: A devastating missile strike by the US on a school in Minab, Iran, has led to the tragic loss of over 150 lives, including 123 innocent children. Investigations uncovered serious issues in the military’s targeting tactics, pointing to outdated intelligence and a lack of comprehensive civilian harm evaluations. The AI-powered Maven Smart System was crucial in target assessments.

item.title: SC flags ‘false’ POCSO cases in marital disputes, bars immediate arrest of accused parent
item.description: The Supreme Court has stressed the need for cautious evaluations prior to immediate arrests under the POCSO Act. They underscored the crucial role of expert child assessments when parents are under scrutiny. In matrimonial conflicts, police are urged to confirm relationships before making arrests. The court expressed concern over the rising incidents of false allegations in family disputes, highlighting the importance of in-depth investigations prioritizing children's welfare.

item.title: Chess Olympiad: India miss chance to close in as Gukesh draws; Savitha saves women’s day
item.description: Gukesh pushed hard but was held to a draw by Azerbaijan’s Mahammad Muradli as India missed a chance to close the gap on the Chess Olympiad leaders. Uzbekistan and Germany lead the open section with 14 points. In the women’s event, Savitha Shri extended her winning streak to seven, rescuing India against Kazakhstan and keeping their title hopes alive.

item.title: Xi Jinping tests Donald Trump with 'Thucydides Trap'
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping asserted that the US and China should work together to avoid conflict. He emphasized that China's rise does not have to threaten the United States' position. Despite past confrontational rhetoric, President Trump responded positively, highlighting their relationship. Critics remain skeptical, arguing that China's military expansion poses significant risks. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stressed the importance of engaging with China amidst these challenges.

item.title: Rahul attacks Centre over EC-SIR row; BJP calls it 'jooth ki goonj'
item.description: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has intensified accusations against the government and the Election Commission regarding electoral integrity. He demands the immediate resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, citing evidence of electoral manipulation. Concerns regarding unresolved objections from Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi further bolster his claims. The BJP has responded by rejecting his allegations and challenging his assertions about anti-incumbency.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Tata Sons tells Noel Tata Chandrasekaran reappointment was legally valid: Report
item.description: Tata Sons has asserted the legal validity of N Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman. The company cited legal opinions supporting the decision against the Tata Trusts' allegations of governance breaches. A pending vote on his directorship is crucial for his continuation in the role. Complications arise as regulatory restrictions limit the Sir Ratan Tata Trust's voting decisions.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Father's 'affairs', property fear: Why Kanpur millionaire's son ordered the hit job
item.description: Subrat Manocha has been arrested for allegedly plotting the murder of his father, Vineet Manocha, over financial concerns. The father was killed in his apartment in Kanpur, and investigations led to multiple arrests, including his daughter-in-law Shalu. Police have found evidence indicating Subrat's gambling debts and motive linked to his father's relationships. Initial plans to disguise the murder as accidental were abandoned as the plot unfolded.
